correctness.rationale: For a rotation through α the joint squared loss is 2(sin²(2α)+ε²cos²(2α)), with optimum 2ε². In the random eigenbasis the conjugation uses the direction of (g1,εg2); isotropy of (g1,g2) gives the stated one-trial law, whose survival is powered by L. Independently, writing t for the distance of the best folded angle to π/2 yields density L(2/π)^L t^(L−1) and normalized squared loss (sin²t+ε²cos²t)^−1. For L=1 the tangent substitution gives 1/ε. For L=2, the squared-moment integral near t=0 differs from the integral of t/(t²+ε²) by a uniformly bounded amount, giving the 8/π² normalized log coefficient. The integrable limits for L≥3 follow from sin t≥2t/π. At L=3 integration by parts gives ∫ t² csc²t dt=π log 2 over [0,π/2]; at L=2 the first-moment integral uses ∫ t csc t dt=2 Catalan over the same interval. L=1's first moment is the complete elliptic integral; subtracting the regularizing integrand 1/sqrt(t²+ε²) gives the log(4/ε) asymptotic. Thus the constants refer to rates at fixed L, not failure of finite-noise moment existence. Read verify_rjd.py without executing it. `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py` (section 2; mpmath and SymPy) corroborates the normalized constants by angle-density integration; the proof uses integrable domination and the explicit endpoint comparison, not numerical extrapolation.
